newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major defeats censure motion over BSE.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major defeats censure motion over BSE.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major on Monday defeated a censure motion proposed by the main opposition Labour party on his government's handling of the crisis over BSE, or mad cow disease.

The lower House of Commons rejected by 320 votes to 307 a Labour motion critical of Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg. Defeat for Major would have triggered a confidence vote that could have forced the prime minister to call an early election.

Major's government, which has no overall majority in the 651-seat lower House of Commons, had earlier worked hard for its victory by wooing a crucial group of members of parliament from Northern Ireland who in effect hold the balance of power.

Hogg, with Major's approval, promised the nine members of the Ulster Unionist party that he would soon submit proposals to the European Commission for a partial lifting of the European Union's worldwide ban on British beef exports -- a move that would particularly help Northern Ireland's beef farmers.
The EU imposed the ban last March because of evidence that the invariably fatal mad cow disease, or bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), could be transmitted to humans.

Major's victory means he can still hope for now to soldier on until his preferred general election date, said to be May 1. But he faces more trouble on February 27, when Labour is tipped to win a by-election in northwest England that would put the ruling Conservatives into a minority in parliament.
